observation.visible_scene: A macro close-up against a pure black background. A pale wooden matchstick enters horizontally from the right edge, its dark, unburned head resting near the center of the frame. Directly below the match head stands a vertical, green braided wick. A bright yellow-white flame burns just above the match head / wick-top junction, with a faint grey smoke haze drifting to its left.
visible_changes: The matchstick and the green wick hold fixed positions throughout the excerpt (head at roughly the same pixel location, wick vertical below it); there is no object translation and no evident camera movement.

The flame's morphology changes over time: in the early frames it is a shorter, slightly left-leaning tongue of fire, while in later frames it stretches taller and more vertical, its tip reaching and crossing the top edge of the frame, accompanied by a more pronounced grey smoke plume on the left.

A small, intense white glowing spot emerges at the left rim of the match head around t=0.56 s (frame 8) and persists through the middle frames before fading, while the body of the head remains dark and charred-looking.
The overall brightness and vertical extent of the luminous region above the head increase as the segment progresses.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the wick flame was originally lit and what holds the wick in place (only its very top is visible).
Whether the match head fully ignites and the stick burns after this excerpt ends.
The state of the scene before t=0.0 s and after t=3.2 s.
uncertain_details: Whether the dominant flame is fed by the green wick, by the heated match head, or by both; the base of the flame coincides with the head/wick junction so the exact fuel source is not separable from these frames.
Whether the white spot on the head is ignition of the match compound or a specular highlight on a hot surface.
The precise moment of head ignition, since the glow develops gradually rather than appearing in a single frame.
